A passive element in electrical engineering is one that does not produce or amplify energy but can only store or dissipate it.  
A resistor is passive because it dissipates energy as heat.  
A bulb (incandescent lamp) is essentially a resistor when operating — it dissipates electrical energy as light and heat, but does not generate energy, so it is also passive.  
Thus, both are passive elements.
